violations.why: writer1_isr (prio 3) can preempt closer2_isr between its two reads of test_global_var1, so they may see different values.
writer2_isr (prio 4) can preempt closer2_isr between the two reads, so they may differ.
The increment is a non-atomic read-modify-write. writer3_isr (prio 5) can preempt it, and its write is then overwritten.
closer1_isr has equal priority and can preempt closer2_isr between its write and its check. It can also reset the value through i8xx_tco_write.
Another equal-priority closer ISR can preempt between the write and the check and change the value.
closer3_isr's check in release and its later reset can be split by a preempting closer ISR that writes the variable, so the reset overwrites that write.
closer1_isr writes 'V' and then reads it in i8xx_tco_write. An equal-priority closer ISR can preempt in between and overwrite the buffer.
